title: Regional tripwires and graceful cutover policy for tenant-tier routing
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Implement region-aware automated tripwires and a graceful cutover policy that protects downstream model serving pools and preserves SLA for higher-tier customers. This ticket covers: 1) signal definitions (429 surge, persistent timeouts, error-rate and tail-latency thresholds), 2) per-tenant-tier gating (free/starter/enterprise), 3) region-level capacity signaling and cutover logic, and 4) an orchestration for circuit state transitions (Closed -> Open -> Half-Open -> Closed) with cooldowns and progressive routing cutover percentages. The policy must be configurable via Console and expose metrics for decision reasoning.

Motivation: We have recurring regional incidents where a sudden influx causes 429s and elevated p95 latency; current reactive fallbacks either overcorrect (evict all traffic) or are too slow. We need deterministic, observable behavior that isolates overloaded pools while honouring higher tier SLAs and enabling safe recovery.

Key design points:
- Signals: sliding-window based counts and rates: 429 rate (per-route, per-tenant, per-region) over 30s/5m windows; consecutive request timeouts threshold; p95 and p99 latency increase relative to baseline (relative delta > 2x over rolling 5m).
- Thresholding: use two-tier thresholds: bump (warning) and trip (protect). Bump triggers additional telemetry/trace capture and a soft-throttle; trip opens protective measures. Thresholds can be absolute or baseline-relative, configurable by route and tenant tier.
- Circuit states: Closed (normal), Degraded (soft cutover, e.g., 20% traffic reroute), Open (aggressive cutover to fallback model variant/region), Probe (half-open - small % traffic allowed back to original path). State transitions include exponential cooldowns and backoff ramp for repeated flapping detection.
- Tier routing: enterprise tenants get longer cooldown windows and higher tolerance; free-tier defaults to aggressive protection. Admin-configurable per-tenant policy overrides via Console.
- Region selection: prefer same-region capacity; when region is unhealthy, weighted cutover to the next-fallback region with cost and latency cost model that factors into routing decision.
- Fallback model variants: prefer quantized / lower-throughput variants as intermediate step (instead of full regional cutover) when model-variant-compatible to reduce latency-c financial trade-offs.
- Observability: expose decision reasons in traces and Console: trip_reason, metric_snapshot (counts, rates), state_history, and suggested remediation. Emit alert events to PagerDuty for high-priority trips affecting enterprise customers.
- Config & API: new policy DSL in routing config: trip_conditions, bump_conditions, cutover_plan (percentages, target_variant/region), cooldowns, tier_overrides. Backwards-compatible defaults should be applied when policy absent.

Non-goals: global autoscaling improvements, new kernel selection logic, or KV cache internals (these are separate initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: Policy can be attached to any route and scoped by tenant tier and region
Trips fire deterministically in staging when injected 429/timeouts using load test harness
Console shows trip decision details for each fired trip and allows manual override
Cutover follows configured percentages and transitions through Probe state with metrics confirming reduced error-rate in target pools
Enterprise tenants maintain configured SLOs during protected cutovers in tested scenarios
Automated tests validate state machine transitions and cooldown/backoff behaviour
tasks: Design RFC for policy DSL and state machine (owner: Marco)
Implement trip detection library (30s/5m windows) and expose as routing signals (owner: Priya)
Integrate policy evaluation in router: apply cutover percentages and variant selection (owner: Marco)
Console UI: policy editor and trip inspector (owner: Diego)
Load test scenarios and chaos injection in staging (owner: SRE team)
Create runbook and PagerDuty routing for enterprise-impacting trips (owner: Ops)
Add e2e tests and unit tests for state transitions (owner: QA)
Document default thresholds and migration notes (owner: Docs)
notes: Initial threshold proposal: bump=429 rate > 1% of requests in 30s; trip=429 rate > 5% in 30s or p95 latency > 2x baseline over 5m
Plan to reuse metrics exported by runtime SLO agent; may need a small extension to tag metrics by tenant-tier
Discussed with Product: enterprise tier should be opt-in for aggressive protection to avoid unexpected reroutes
Risk: misconfigured cutover percentages could cause user-perceived regressions; we will introduce safe defaults and a preview mode
